page.metaTitle: Cyber Monday Deal Tracking & Online Sale Alerts | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Cyber Monday deal tracking with real-time alerts on price drops, restocks, and limited-stock deals across every major online retailer.
page.subtitle: Catch Cyber Monday deals as they activate. Five-minute checks across every retailer, alerts the moment your thresholds hit.
page.intro: Cyber Monday is more online-tech-heavy than Black Friday, with software, hardware, and SaaS subscriptions all running their own deal windows. The deal density is high; the time-to-sellout is short. Five-minute monitor checks across the retailers and platforms you care about deliver alerts inside the sellout window.

setup.title: Extend Black Friday monitors into Sunday night
setup.body: Many "Black Friday" monitors carry the same items through Cyber Monday. If you already have monitors set up for the weekend, leave them running.

setup.title: Add software and SaaS deal pages
setup.body: Cyber Monday is the heaviest software-deal weekend of the year. Add the pricing pages of any tools you're considering — the discount activation triggers an alert.

setup.title: Track limited-stock electronics deals
setup.body: Best Buy doorbusters, Amazon lightning deals, Target online exclusives. Five-minute checks with SMS alerts.

page.limits: Cyber Monday traffic stresses retailer infrastructure. Some sites have rolling outages on Monday morning that affect monitor reliability. Multi-region uptime checks help confirm whether a missed alert is a monitor issue or a temporary site issue.

faq.q: How is Cyber Monday tracking different from Black Friday tracking?
faq.a: The mechanics are the same. The product mix shifts — Cyber Monday leans heavier on online-only and software deals. Most users run the same monitors through both windows with adjusted frequencies.
Yes. Most software pricing pages are public. Set the monitor on the pricing page with the criterion "alert me on any price change" and you'll catch the deal activation and the rollback.
Lightning deal pages have a rolling product carousel; tracking the page itself catches when a target product cycles into the carousel.
